title: Check: API objects and YAML
description: Five questions on the shape every object shares and what the fields mean.

questions.prompt: Which top-level fields does essentially every Kubernetes object carry? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation: apiVersion, kind, metadata and spec are the shape you write. `status` exists too, but the cluster owns it - you do not author it.

questions.prompt: What is the difference between `spec` and `status`?

options.text: `spec` is what you want; `status` is what the cluster observes
They are two names for the same thing

questions.explanation: You write `spec`. Controllers write `status`. The whole system is the loop that tries to make the second match the first.

questions.prompt: A Deployment manifest uses `apiVersion: v1`. What happens?

options.text: It works - v1 is the default for everything
It is rejected: Deployment lives in apps/v1
It is silently converted to apps/v1

questions.explanation: apiVersion names the group and version the kind belongs to. Deployments are in the apps group, so `apps/v1`.

questions.prompt: Write the command that lists the fields available under a Deployment's spec.
questions.explanation: `kubectl explain` is the schema reference that is always available, including in the exam terminal.

questions.prompt: Where does an object's namespace belong in the manifest?

options.text: At the top level, beside kind
It cannot be set in the manifest

questions.explanation: Namespace is metadata, alongside name, labels and annotations.
